query: Consider the following context: The combination of elevated temperature and tribo-corrosion leads to the accelerated degradation of structural components used in many extreme environments. Recently developed high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements have the potential for superior degradation resistance compared with presently used structural alloys. In that context, which material can be used for superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with optimized composition, specifically the combination of FeCrNiCoMn with the addition of 5 at.% aluminum, will exhibit superior tribo-corrosion degradation resistance compared to conventional structural alloys.
generation.intervention: Optimizing the composition of HEAs by selecting elements that enhance corrosion and wear resistance, specifically adding 5 at.% of aluminum to the FeCrNiCoMn alloy. The addition of 5 at.% aluminum is expected to enhance the formation of a stable alumina layer, which has been shown to reduce wear and corrosion in similar alloy systems.
generation.conditions: Elevated temperature (500°C) and tribo-corrosion environment with a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s and a normal load of 50 N. The sliding speed of 0.1 m/s and normal load of 50 N were selected to simulate the typical operating conditions of structural components in extreme environments, where high contact pressures and moderate sliding speeds are common.
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary segregation of alloying elements
generation.mechanism: Enhanced corrosion and wear resistance due to the formation of a stable oxide layer and reduced grain boundary diffusion. At elevated temperatures, the stable oxide layer formed on the surface of the optimized HEA is expected to remain intact, reducing wear and corrosion, while the reduced grain boundary diffusion minimizes the transport of corrosive species to the grain boundaries.
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in wear rate from 10 mm³/Nm to 7 mm³/Nm and a 25% reduction in corrosion rate from 5 mm/year to 3.75 mm/year compared to conventional structural alloys (e.g., 316L stainless steel).
generation.baseline: Conventional structural alloys (e.g., 316L stainless steel) with a wear rate of 10 mm³/Nm and a corrosion rate of 5 mm/year
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear and corrosion rates may vary depending on the specific operating conditions and the microstructure of the optimized HEA.

falsification_experiment.design: Tribocorrosion test with a ball-on-disk setup
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate is not at least 25% lower and the corrosion rate is not at least 20% lower than those of the conventional structural alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
